title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM‑Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine), a single shared initial candidate per task was generated by gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced task-encoded workflow policies and could trigger ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; paired contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We clarify the confirmatory binary outcome definition, present a compact nearest-work comparison, interpret the degenerate ceiling result, and give artifact-grounded methodological recommendations for follow-up confirmatory designs.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into executable network configuration. However, syntactically plausible outputs can violate stateful workflow invariants (for example, MTU changes that must be applied while an interface is down, or make-before-break uplink switchover rules); such semantic failures often appear only in closed-loop execution. Prior work therefore recommends integrate‑and‑verify patterns—executable emulation, formal verification, or bounded guardrails—so that generated candidates are validated before enactment. We conducted a preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) to isolate the marginal effect of an executable emulator validator plus a bounded repair policy on identical generator outputs. The central confirmatory question was: does adding an executable emulator validator (and one repair iteration budget) reduce emulator-observed semantic failures compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow when the generator output is held constant across paired episodes? Our choice of a shared-initial-candidate paired design maximizes internal validity for measuring validator/repair impact but, as preregistered, risks leaving repair unused when the generator is well-calibrated for the selected task bank. We report the exact execution accounting, a formal definition of the binary confirmatory outcome used in hypothesis testing, representative diagnostic examples drawn from archived scoring artifacts, and concrete design recommendations for future confirmatory studies that aim to measure repair utility.
sections.related_work:
Two research streams motivate this study. (1) Executable and closed-loop benchmarks and verification tools show that token/syntax checks miss sequencing and stateful errors; recent executable-benchmark efforts demonstrate that closed-loop emulation reveals operational failure classes (e.g., make-before-break, group-availability violations) not detectable by static checks [https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23179; https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.22513]. (2) Architectural proposals for tool-augmented agentic NetOps and bounded-autonomy guardrails advocate generate→validate→repair or veto layers to improve operational safety [https://openalex.org/W7155247165; https://openalex.org/W7161354925].

Nearest‑work comparison (compact):
- Protogeros et al., "Benchmarking LLM‑Driven Network Configuration Repair" (arXiv 2604.22513): generator‑centric benchmark; independent per-condition generation; focuses on repair incidence across sampled generations. Difference: our paired shared‑generation design holds generator outputs identical to isolate validator marginal effects.
- NetConfArena (arXiv 2608.23179): executable closed‑loop tasks; evaluates agentic behaviors in emulation. Difference: NetConfArena emphasizes end‑to‑end agent evaluation under variable generation; our contribution is a preregistered paired test that isolates validator/repair effects on identical candidates.
- Aether / tool‑augmented architectures (W7155247165, W7161354925): propose verifier/digital‑twin integration and guardrails. Difference: we implement a deterministic emulator validator and preregistered repair budget to quantify the marginal contribution of validator+repair for shared generator outputs.

This study is therefore complementary to prior work: we do not attempt exhaustive cross‑model ranking or broad production validation; instead we present a tightly controlled, artifact‑rich paired test that reveals how experimental design choices (shared vs independent generation) change the opportunity for repair to act.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental plan. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1 prior to execution. Key preregistered design elements: paired‑binary confirmatory design with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class), a shared_initial_generation stage (one LLM call per pair), primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar, and bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729). The preregistration specified deterministic harness controls (emulator resets, container checksums), contamination/exclusion rules, and a repair budget of ≤1 repair per guarded episode. The preregistration SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest (0bfc96e9afceed579f04a06dcbad2387ee4acca970559d9a4faa165893f4fe50).

Task generation and validator semantics. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task payload includes initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural‑language intent, and an explicit required_sequence that the validator checks as structured constraints (examples: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints). The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) in an emulated state checker. The validator emits a structured validator_trace with validation_before, validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy was triggered only when validator.violation_count>0 and allowed at most one repair iteration; repair prompts and provider traces were archived when generated.

Formal binary outcome (confirmatory label). The binary pass/fail label used in the McNemar test was defined pre‑execution and implemented deterministically by the scorer: (1) If validator.violation_count > 0 (validator reported at least one semantic/sequence/workflow violation) then outcome = FAIL. (2) Else, if validator.violation_count == 0 AND normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer then outcome = PASS. (3) Else (validator.violation_count == 0 but normalized_response != normalized_reference_answer), outcome = FAIL. Tie‑breaking: structured validator verdicts take precedence over superficial token similarity when both are available. This mapping is the exact logic applied in the archived scoring artifacts (scorer_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation).

Shared‑generation rationale and consequences. For each task we produced a single generator output (declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini) and applied the same candidate to both baseline and guarded scoring pipelines. This isolates validator/repair marginal effects by removing generator sampling variance. The trade‑off is that if the generator produces valid candidates for the curated task bank, repaired behavior cannot appear because the guard never triggers—an outcome anticipated and discussed in the preregistration.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcome. The run completed per the preregistered contract: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition summaries (analysis/condition_summary.csv) record baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired‑difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes and violation_count = 0 in every guarded validation_after.

Per‑topology counts (preregistered partition of 40 tasks each): Edge: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Core: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40; Leaf–spine: baseline 40/40, guarded 40/40. Representative scoring artifact example (artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json) shows normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer and validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; the guarded artifact execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json shows validator_trace.repair_applied = false. Because no guarded episodes reported violations, preregistered secondary endpoints that measure repair incidence and repair‑call counts are vacuous in this run.

Statistical interpretation of the degenerate contingency. A paired design with zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0) yields an exact McNemar p = 1.0 and a degenerate bootstrap CI at the observed difference (0.00). This result does not imply that a guarded pipeline could not help under other generator or task distributions; it indicates that, for the chosen task bank and shared prompt/generator setup, the generator outputs already satisfied the validator's structured workflow checks for every task in the sample.
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling occurred and what it implies. The shared‑generation paired design answers a mechanistic question: for a given generator output, can a validator+bounded repair change the outcome relative to a bare suggestion? In this experiment the generator outputs were, empirically, valid for the curated synthetic task bank; consequently the guard never exercised repair and could not reduce semantic failures versus baseline. The degenerate confirmatory result therefore reflects both an internally consistent execution (no contamination or technical exclusions) and a limitation of the selected design for demonstrating repair utility under low generator error incidence.

Design recommendations for follow‑ups (artifact‑grounded): (1) Allow independent per‑condition generation for a prespecified subsample to increase the chance of generator‑induced violations while preserving paired blocking elsewhere; (2) Stratify confirmatory sampling on manifest difficulty metadata (for example, restrict to tasks with dependency_rule_count ≥ 2 or tasks labeled 'very_hard'); (3) Introduce controlled prompt perturbations (the preregistration included exploratory perturbation variants) to systematically increase generator variance; (4) Expand exploratory repair budgets (multiple repair iterations) to study convergence and cost.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: high—deterministic provisioning, archived provider audits, zero exclusions, and reconciled accounting. Construct validity: moderate—the validator enforces structured workflow policies encoded in task payloads, but it simplifies vendor heterogeneity and partial observability present in many production networks. External validity: limited—synthetic deterministic tasks, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy constrain generalization to diverse production settings. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power assumptions (expected baseline ≈ 0.40) were violated by the observed baseline = 0.00, rendering the confirmatory McNemar test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We performed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) that holds generator outputs constant to measure the marginal effect of an executable validator plus a bounded repair policy. All shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired difference of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The principal scientific contribution is methodological and practical: we demonstrate how a preregistered, artifact‑rich paired design can cleanly isolate validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider audits, reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the confirmatory test is degenerate. Archived artifacts permit targeted follow‑ups that relax shared‑generation, increase task difficulty, compare generator families, and expand repair budgets to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
